Exam Practice 1

In paper order.

Q1Share $223.60 in the ratio 6 : 7Right · 2 marks · Number
Question

Isaac and Syah share $223.60 in the ratio 6 : 7. Find the amount each receives. [2]

The question as printed
1 part=223.60÷13=17.20Isaac=6×17.20=103.20Syah=7×17.20=120.40\begin{aligned} 1 \text{ part} &= 223.60 \div 13 = 17.20\\ \text{Isaac} &= 6 \times 17.20 = 103.20\\ \text{Syah} &= 7 \times 17.20 = 120.40 \end{aligned}

Answer: Isaac $103.20, Syah $120.40

Q25 sin w° = 3, two values of w from 0 to 180Right · 2 marks · Trigonometry
Question

5 sin w° = 3. Find two possible values of w in the range 0 ≤ w ≤ 180. [2]

The question as printed
sin⁡w∘=35=0.6w=sin⁡−1(0.6)=36.87∘w=180∘−36.87∘=143.13∘\begin{aligned} \sin w^\circ &= \frac{3}{5} = 0.6\\ w &= \sin^{-1}(0.6) = 36.87^\circ\\ w &= 180^\circ - 36.87^\circ = 143.13^\circ \end{aligned}

Answer: w = 36.9 or w = 143.1

Q3(2y − 1) ÷ 3 − (y + 1) ÷ 6 as one fractionRight · 2 marks · Algebra
Question

Write (2y − 1)/3 − (y + 1)/6 as a single fraction in its simplest form. [2]

The question as printed
2y−13−y+16=2(2y−1)−(y+1)6=4y−2−y−16=3y−36=3(y−1)6=y−12\begin{aligned} \frac{2y-1}{3}-\frac{y+1}{6} &= \frac{2(2y-1)-(y+1)}{6}\\ &= \frac{4y-2-y-1}{6} = \frac{3y-3}{6}\\ &= \frac{3(y-1)}{6} = \frac{y-1}{2} \end{aligned}

Answer: (y − 1) ÷ 2

Q4Prime powersWrong before · 3 marks · Number

Wrong before. 13 Sep: (b) left blank. The same skill was right on his own on 30 Sep (EP3 Q4(b)).

Question

(a) P = a⁶ × b³ × c⁹, where a, b and c are prime numbers. Explain why P is a perfect cube. [1]

(b) Y = 3⁴ × 5³ × 2⁵. (i) The number T = Y × m is a perfect square. Find the smallest possible integer value of m. [1]

(ii) Z = 3⁶ × 5⁴ × 2³. Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of Y and Z as a product of its prime factors. [1]

The question as printed

(a) P = a⁶ × b³ × c⁹. Every power is a multiple of 3, so P is a cube:

P=(a2×b×c3)3P = (a^2 \times b \times c^3)^3

(b)(i) Y = 3⁴ × 5³ × 2⁵. A perfect square needs every power even. 5³ needs one more 5; 2⁵ needs one more 2.

m=5×2=10m = 5 \times 2 = 10

(b)(ii) Z = 3⁶ × 5⁴ × 2³. The LCM takes the highest power of each prime.

LCM=25×36×54\text{LCM} = 2^5 \times 3^6 \times 5^4

Answer: (b)(i) m = 10   (b)(ii) 2⁵ × 3⁶ × 5⁴

Q5$8000 at 0.5% per month, compoundRight · 3 marks · Number
Question

Jay invests $8000 at a rate of 0.5% per month compound interest.

(a) Explain why the first year's interest is not 6% of $8000. [1]

(b) Calculate the value of his investment at the end of 12 months. [2]

The question as printed

(a) Each month's interest also earns interest, so the year's interest is more than 6%: $493.42 against $480.

8000×(1+0.5100)12=8493.428000 \times \left(1+\frac{0.5}{100}\right)^{12} = 8493.42

Answer: (b) $8493.42

Q6x² − 16x + 54 = (x − h)² + kWrong before · 3 marks · Algebra

Wrong before. 13 Sep: h = 4, k = 54. Right on the retry, 19 Sep.

Question

The expression x² − 16x + 54 is equivalent to (x − h)² + k.

(a) Find the value of h and the value of k. [2]

(b) The curve y = x² − 16x + 54 is drawn. Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of the curve. [1]

The question as printed
x2−16x+54=(x−8)2−64+54=(x−8)2−10\begin{aligned} x^2-16x+54 &= (x-8)^2-64+54\\ &= (x-8)^2-10 \end{aligned}

Answer: h = 8, k = −10. Line of symmetry x = 8

Q7P(−2, 3), Q(a, b), gradient 1 ÷ 4. Express a in terms of bWrong before · 2 marks · Coordinates

Wrong before. 13 Sep: gradient upside down. Right on his own, 19 Sep.

Question

P is the point (−2, 3) and Q is the point (a, b). The gradient of the line PQ is 1/4. Express a in terms of b. Give your answer in its simplest form. [2]

The question as printed

Up over across: change in y on top.

b−3a−(−2)=144(b−3)=a+2a=4b−14\begin{aligned} \frac{b-3}{a-(-2)} &= \frac{1}{4}\\ 4(b-3) &= a+2\\ a &= 4b-14 \end{aligned}

Answer: a = 4b − 14

Q8PercentagesWrong before · 4 marks · Number

Wrong before, not practised since. 13 Sep: (b) left blank.

Question

(a) Mikail has 36 Pokémon trading cards. He increases his number of cards by 150%. Find the number of cards he has now. [2]

(b) Lukas collects football cards. 36% of his cards are from the Spanish League. 56.25% of the remaining cards are from the English League. The remaining 84 cards are from the French League. How many cards does Lukas have in total? [2]

The question as printed

(a) 36 cards increased by 150%:

36×250100=9036 \times \frac{250}{100} = 90

(b) 36% Spanish, 56.25% of the REMAINING English, 84 French:

Remaining=100%−36%=64%English=56.25%×64%=36%French=64%−36%=28%28%=84Total=84÷0.28=300\begin{aligned} \text{Remaining} &= 100\% - 36\% = 64\%\\ \text{English} &= 56.25\% \times 64\% = 36\%\\ \text{French} &= 64\% - 36\% = 28\%\\ 28\% &= 84\\ \text{Total} &= 84 \div 0.28 = 300 \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) 90 cards   (b) 300 cards

Q9Car $170 000 on hire purchase: 18% deposit, 84 payments of $1935Wrong before · 4 marks · Number

Wrong before. 13 Sep: divided by 193 140 instead of 170 000. Right on his own both ways, 19 Sep.

Question

The cash price of a car is $170 000. Aqil buys the car using hire purchase. He pays a deposit of 18% of the cash price plus 84 equal monthly payments of $1935.

(a) Calculate the total amount that Aqil pays for the car. [2]

(b) Express the extra cost of using hire purchase as a percentage of the cash price. [2]

The question as printed
Deposit=0.18×170000=30600Payments=84×1935=162540Total=30600+162540=193140Extra=193140−170000=2314023140170000×100=13.6%\begin{aligned} \text{Deposit} &= 0.18 \times 170000 = 30600\\ \text{Payments} &= 84 \times 1935 = 162540\\ \text{Total} &= 30600 + 162540 = 193140\\ \text{Extra} &= 193140 - 170000 = 23140\\ \frac{23140}{170000} \times 100 &= 13.6\% \end{aligned}

Percentage of the CASH PRICE: 170 000 on the bottom.

Answer: (a) $193 140   (b) 13.6%

Q10IndicesStill open · 5 marks · Indices

(b) still open. 13 Sep: (a) letters not cubed, (b) u = 16. (a) right on his own 19 Sep. (b) the bracket line after taking out 3⁶ has never been written.

Question

(a) Simplify (4a⁶ ÷ b⁴) to the power −3/2, leaving your answer in positive index form. [2]

(b) 49 × 3⁶ + 32 × 9³ = 3ᵘ. Use the laws of indices to find the value of u. Show your working. [3]

The question as printed

(a) (4a⁶ ÷ b⁴) to the power −3 ÷ 2, positive indices. Flip, then root, then cube, on the number AND every letter.

(4a6b4)−32=(b44a6)32=b6432a9=b68a9\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{4a^6}{b^4}\right)^{-\frac{3}{2}} &= \left(\frac{b^4}{4a^6}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}\\ &= \frac{b^{6}}{4^{\frac32}a^{9}} = \frac{b^6}{8a^9} \end{aligned}

(b) 49 × 3⁶ + 32 × 9³ = 3ᵘ. Take the shared power out ONCE.

32×93=32×3649×36+32×36=36(49+32)=36×81=36×34=310\begin{aligned} 32 \times 9^3 &= 32 \times 3^6\\ 49 \times 3^6 + 32 \times 3^6 &= 3^6(49+32)\\ &= 3^6 \times 81 = 3^6 \times 3^4 = 3^{10} \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) b⁶ ÷ (8a⁹)   (b) u = 10

Q11Factorise completelyWrong before · 4 marks · Algebra

Wrong before, not practised since. 13 Sep: (a) a sign lost, 3(y − 2)(2y − 1).

Question

Factorise completely.

(a) 6y² − 9y − 6 [2]

(b) 2pq − r + 2pr − q [2]

The question as printed
6y2−9y−6=3(2y2−3y−2)=3(2y+1)(y−2)2pq+2pr−q−r=2p(q+r)−(q+r)=(2p−1)(q+r)\begin{aligned} 6y^2-9y-6 &= 3(2y^2-3y-2) = 3(2y+1)(y-2)\\ 2pq+2pr-q-r &= 2p(q+r)-(q+r) = (2p-1)(q+r) \end{aligned}

Expand back to check the signs.

Answer: (a) 3(2y + 1)(y − 2)   (b) (2p − 1)(q + r)

Q1212 pens, 7 highlighters, 6 pencils; m highlighters added; P(highlighter) = 0.6Right · 2 marks · Probability
Question

A bag contains 12 pens, 7 highlighters and 6 pencils. Another m highlighters are added to the bag. The probability of picking a highlighter is now 0.6. Find the value of m. [2]

The question as printed
7+m25+m=0.67+m=15+0.6m0.4m=8m=20\begin{aligned} \frac{7+m}{25+m} &= 0.6\\ 7+m &= 15+0.6m\\ 0.4m &= 8\\ m &= 20 \end{aligned}

Answer: m = 20

Q13Simplify (3y² + y − 10) ÷ (y² − 4)Right · 3 marks · Algebra
Question

Simplify (3y² + y − 10) ÷ (y² − 4). [3]

The question as printed
3y2+y−10y2−4=(3y−5)(y+2)(y−2)(y+2)=3y−5y−2\frac{3y^2+y-10}{y^2-4} = \frac{(3y-5)(y+2)}{(y-2)(y+2)} = \frac{3y-5}{y-2}

Answer: (3y − 5) ÷ (y − 2)

Q14Why (p − 2)² − (p + 8)(p − 2) is a multiple of 5Wrong before · 3 marks · Algebra

Wrong before, not practised since. 13 Sep: wrote 5(−2p + 10), and the sentence only said "there is a 5".

Question

Explain why (p − 2)² − (p + 8)(p − 2) is a multiple of 5 for all integer values of p. [3]

The question as printed

Minus a bracket: every sign inside flips.

(p2−4p+4)−(p2+6p−16)=−10p+20=5(4−2p)\begin{aligned} &(p^2-4p+4)-(p^2+6p-16)\\ &= -10p+20\\ &= 5(4-2p) \end{aligned}

Answer: 5 × (4 − 2p), and 4 − 2p is an integer, so it is a multiple of 5.

Q15Sketch y = −(x + 2)(x − 5)Right · 2 marks · Graphs
Question

Sketch the graph of y = −(x + 2)(x − 5) on the axes given. Indicate clearly the points where the graph crosses the axes. [2]

The question as printed
y=0:x=−2 or x=5x=0:y=−(2)(−5)=10\begin{aligned} y=0: &\quad x=-2 \text{ or } x=5\\ x=0: &\quad y=-(2)(-5)=10 \end{aligned}

Answer: n-shape (minus in front), crossing the x-axis at −2 and 5 and the y-axis at 10.

Q16Pyramid 20 cm deep; sand fills half the volume; find x, the empty depthRight · 3 marks · Similar solids
Question

Diagram A shows a square pyramid containing some sand. Diagram B shows the cross-section of the pyramid and sand: the pyramid is 20 cm deep and the empty space at the top is x cm deep. The volume of sand in the pyramid is equal to the volume of the empty space in the pyramid. Find the value of x. [3]

The question as printed

Similar shapes: volume ratio = (length ratio)³.

(20−x20)3=1220−x20=0.53=0.793720−x=15.874x=4.13\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{20-x}{20}\right)^3 &= \frac12\\ \frac{20-x}{20} &= \sqrt[3]{0.5} = 0.7937\\ 20-x &= 15.874\\ x &= 4.13 \end{aligned}

Answer: x = 4.13

Q17Equilateral ABC: AC = 4x + 5y − 3, AB = 5x + y, BC = 16y − xWrong before · 5 marks · Algebra

Wrong before, not practised since. 13 Sep: (b) wrote 5(5) + 2 = 12.

Question

ABC is an equilateral triangle. AC = (4x + 5y − 3) cm and AB = (5x + y) cm.

(a) Express x in terms of y. [2]

(b) Given that BC = (16y − x) cm, find the length of AB. [3]

The question as printed
5x+y=4x+5y−3  ⇒  x=4y−316y−(4y−3)=5(4y−3)+y12y+3=21y−15y=2,x=5AB=5(5)+2=27\begin{aligned} 5x+y &= 4x+5y-3 \;\Rightarrow\; x = 4y-3\\ 16y-(4y-3) &= 5(4y-3)+y\\ 12y+3 &= 21y-15\\ y &= 2,\quad x = 5\\ AB &= 5(5)+2 = 27 \end{aligned}

Could this be true? 5 × 5 = 25, then + 2 = 27.

Answer: (a) x = 4y − 3   (b) AB = 27 cm

Question

A field is in the shape of a triangle ABC. The line AB is drawn in the space provided.

(a) Using a scale of 1 cm to represent 10 m, make an accurate drawing of the field such that AC = 80 m and angle BAC = 65°. [2]

Q19AECB is a parallelogram, FB = 2FD. Prove triangle FED is congruent to triangle BCDStill open · 3 marks · Congruence

Still open. 13 Sep: 2 of 3, the parallel lines not named in the reason. 25 Sep: the same gap three times. On 27 Sep (EP3 Q22, no parallel lines needed) every reason was written.

Question

AECB is a parallelogram. AEF and FDB are straight lines. Given that FB = 2 FD, prove that triangle FED is congruent to triangle BCD. [3]

The question as printed
  • FD = DB (FB = 2FD, so D is the midpoint of FB)
  • Angle FDE = angle BDC (vertically opposite angles)
  • Angle EFD = angle CBD (alternate angles, EF is parallel to CB)

Answer: Triangle FED is congruent to triangle BCD (ASA).

Q2015th and 16th terms are 44 and 47Wrong before · 3 marks · Sequences

Wrong before, not practised since. 13 Sep: counted back one step too many; (b) left blank.

Question

The 15th and 16th terms of a linear sequence are 44 and 47 respectively.

(a) Write down the first three terms of the sequence. [2]

(b) Write down, in terms of n, the nth term of the sequence. [1]

The question as printed
d=47−44=3T1=44−14×3=2Tn=2+3(n−1)=3n−1\begin{aligned} d &= 47-44 = 3\\ T_1 &= 44 - 14 \times 3 = 2\\ T_n &= 2 + 3(n-1) = 3n-1 \end{aligned}

From term 15 back to term 1 is 14 steps, not 15.

Answer: (a) 2, 5, 8   (b) 3n − 1

Q21Prism: AF = FB = 5 cm, AD = 8 cm, AB = 6 cmStill open · 5 marks · 3D trigonometry

(b) still open. 13 Sep and 20 Sep: worked a different triangle, not AEB.

Question

The diagram shows a triangular prism. AF = FB = 5 cm, AD = 8 cm and AB = 6 cm.

(a) Find angle FCB. [2]

(b) Find angle AEB. [3]

The question as printed

Name the triangle first. (a) uses FBC, right angle at B. (b) uses AEB, which is not a face: halve it.

tan⁡∠FCB=58⇒∠FCB=32.0∘EA=EB=52+82=9.434sin⁡12∠AEB=39.434⇒12∠AEB=18.54∘∠AEB=2×18.54∘=37.1∘\begin{aligned} \tan \angle FCB &= \frac{5}{8} \Rightarrow \angle FCB = 32.0^\circ\\ EA = EB &= \sqrt{5^2+8^2} = 9.434\\ \sin \tfrac12\angle AEB &= \frac{3}{9.434} \Rightarrow \tfrac12\angle AEB = 18.54^\circ\\ \angle AEB &= 2 \times 18.54^\circ = 37.1^\circ \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) 32.0°   (b) 37.1°

Q22p is directly proportional to √q; q = 4 when p = 3; find p when q = 8Right · 2 marks · Proportion
Question

p is directly proportional to the square root of q. If q = 4 when p = 3, find the value of p when q = 8. [2]

The question as printed
p=kq3=k4⇒k=1.5p=1.58=4.24\begin{aligned} p &= k\sqrt q\\ 3 &= k\sqrt4 \Rightarrow k = 1.5\\ p &= 1.5\sqrt8 = 4.24 \end{aligned}

Answer: p = 4.24

Question

Given that 0° < A < 180° and cos A = −5/13, without finding the value of A, find the value of

(a) sin A, [1]

(b) cos (A − 90°). [1]

sin⁡A=132−5213=1213cos⁡(A−90∘)=sin⁡A=1213\begin{aligned} \sin A &= \frac{\sqrt{13^2-5^2}}{13} = \frac{12}{13}\\ \cos(A-90^\circ) &= \sin A = \frac{12}{13} \end{aligned}

Q24Regular pentagon ABCDEStill open · 4 marks · Polygons

Still open. 13 Sep: (a) co-interior line not written; (b) 36° instead of 72°. 25 Sep, hexagon version: the angle was right, but the co-interior line still had no angle names.

Question

In the diagram, ABCDE is a regular pentagon.

(a) Show that CE is parallel to BA. [3]

(b) Find angle CBE. [1]

The question as printed
Interior angle=(5−2)×180∘5=108∘∠DCE=180∘−108∘2=36∘∠ECB=108∘−36∘=72∘∠ECB+∠CBA=72∘+108∘=180∘\begin{aligned} \text{Interior angle} &= \frac{(5-2)\times180^\circ}{5} = 108^\circ\\ \angle DCE &= \frac{180^\circ-108^\circ}{2} = 36^\circ\\ \angle ECB &= 108^\circ-36^\circ = 72^\circ\\ \angle ECB + \angle CBA &= 72^\circ+108^\circ = 180^\circ \end{aligned}

(a) Co-interior angles add to 180°, so CE is parallel to BA.

(b) CE = BE (diagonals of a regular pentagon), so triangle BCE is isosceles: angle CBE = angle BCE = 72°.

Answer: (b) 72°

Q4168, perfect cube, LCMStill open · 3 marks · Number

(c) still open. (b) and (c) wrong the first time. (b) right on his own on 30 Sep. (c) right only on the third try.

Question

(a) Express 168 as the product of its prime factors. [1]

(b) Write down the smallest integer p such that 168p is a perfect cube. [1]

(c) Given that the lowest common multiple of 168 and q is 2⁴ × 3 × 7², find the smallest possible value of q. [1]

The question as printed

(b) Top every power up to 3. (c) The LCM is 2⁴ × 3 × 7²: q brings every power 168 cannot reach.

168=23×3×7p=32×72=441q=24×72=784\begin{aligned} 168 &= 2^3\times3\times7\\ p &= 3^2\times7^2 = 441\\ q &= 2^4\times7^2 = 784 \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) 2³ × 3 × 7   (b) p = 441   (c) q = 784

Q512 green, 16 pink, 16 yellow, 20 blue clipsWrong before · 3 marks · Probability

Question

A box contains 12 green, 16 pink, 16 yellow and 20 blue paper clips.

(a) Write down the modal colour. [1]

(b) Find the probability of picking a black paper clip from the box. [1]

(c) Find the probability of picking a paper clip that is not green from the box. [1]

The question as printed
P(not green)=64−1264=5264=1316P(\text{not green}) = \frac{64-12}{64} = \frac{52}{64} = \frac{13}{16}

Q6IndicesWrong before · 3 marks · Indices

Wrong before. Both parts wrong the first time. Right on the retry.

Question

(a) Given that 9ˣ × 2 = 54, find x. [2]

(b) Simplify m n^(3/2) ÷ m⁻¹ n. [1]

The question as printed
9x×2=54⇒9x=2732x=33⇒x=32mn32÷m−1n=m1−(−1) n32−1=m2n12\begin{aligned} 9^x \times 2 &= 54 \Rightarrow 9^x = 27\\ 3^{2x} &= 3^3 \Rightarrow x = \tfrac32\\ mn^{\frac32}\div m^{-1}n &= m^{1-(-1)}\,n^{\frac32-1} = m^2n^{\frac12} \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) x = 3 ÷ 2   (b) m²n^(1/2)

Q76x² + 9x − 27Wrong before · 3 marks · Algebra

Wrong before. (a) left the 3 off the front. Right on the retry.

Question

(a) Factorise 6x² + 9x − 27 completely. [2]

(b) Hence, solve the equation 6x² + 9x − 27 = 0. [1]

The question as printed

Factorise completely keeps the number in front.

6x2+9x−27=3(2x2+3x−9)=3(2x−3)(x+3)x=32 or x=−3\begin{aligned} 6x^2+9x-27 &= 3(2x^2+3x-9) = 3(2x-3)(x+3)\\ x &= \tfrac32 \text{ or } x=-3 \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) 3(2x − 3)(x + 3)   (b) x = 3 ÷ 2 or x = −3

Q8Why the pie chart may be misleadingNot practised · 2 marks · Statistics

Not practised. Never taught.

Question

The pie chart shows the percentage of funds raised by 5 classes during a donation drive for a charity: Class 3A 25%, 3B 40%, 3C 5%, 3D 8%, 3E 22%. Explain why this pie chart may be misleading. [2]

The question as printed

A sector's angle should be percentage × 3.6°.

40%→40×3.6∘=144∘25%→25×3.6∘=90∘\begin{aligned} 40\% &\rightarrow 40 \times 3.6^\circ = 144^\circ\\ 25\% &\rightarrow 25 \times 3.6^\circ = 90^\circ \end{aligned}

Answer: The sectors are not drawn in proportion. Class 3B's 40% is drawn about the same size as Class 3A's 25%.

Q9Lake 18 km² shown as 2 cm² on a mapNot practised · 3 marks · Map scale

Not practised. Never taught.

Question

A lake with an area of 18 km² is represented on a map by an area of 2 cm².

(a) Find the scale of the map in the form 1 : n. [2]

(b) Find the actual length, in kilometres, of a road if it is represented on the map by a length of 4 cm. [1]

The question as printed

Area scale first, then take the square root for the length scale.

2 cm2:18 km21 cm2:9 km21 cm:3 km=300 000 cm4 cm:4×3=12 km\begin{aligned} 2\text{ cm}^2 &: 18\text{ km}^2\\ 1\text{ cm}^2 &: 9\text{ km}^2\\ 1\text{ cm} &: 3\text{ km} = 300\,000\text{ cm}\\ 4\text{ cm} &: 4 \times 3 = 12\text{ km} \end{aligned}

Answer: (a) 1 : 300 000   (b) 12 km

Q10Sequences 1, 4, 9, 16 and 4, 7, 12, 19Wrong before · 3 marks · Sequences

Question

(a) These are the first four terms of a sequence: 1, 4, 9, 16. Write down an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of the sequence. [1]

(b) Hence, find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of the sequence 4, 7, 12, 19. [1]

(c) Explain why 111 is not a term of the second sequence in part (b). [1]

The question as printed
Tn=n2Tn=n2+3n2+3=111⇒n2=108⇒n=10.39\begin{aligned} T_n &= n^2\\ T_n &= n^2+3\\ n^2+3 &= 111 \Rightarrow n^2=108 \Rightarrow n=10.39 \end{aligned}

Q12Area 83.1 cm², AB = 14.5 cm, BC = 17.4 cm: two sizes of angle ABCRight · 3 marks · Trigonometry
Question

The area of triangle ABC is 83.1 cm². AB = 14.5 cm and BC = 17.4 cm. Find the two possible sizes of the angle ABC. [3]

The question as printed
12×14.5×17.4×sin⁡B=83.1sin⁡B=166.2252.3=0.6587B=41.2∘B=180∘−41.2∘=138.8∘\begin{aligned} \tfrac12\times14.5\times17.4\times\sin B &= 83.1\\ \sin B &= \frac{166.2}{252.3} = 0.6587\\ B &= 41.2^\circ\\ B &= 180^\circ-41.2^\circ = 138.8^\circ \end{aligned}

Q133x − 13 ≤ x + 1 < (4x + 2) ÷ 3Wrong before · 4 marks · Inequalities

Nearly right. Solved on his own, but wrote 13 + 1 = 12 and left the number line out.

Question

Solve the inequalities 3x − 13 ≤ x + 1 < (4x + 2)/3. Show your solution on the number line provided. [4]

The question as printed

Split into two. The sign flips only when you divide by a negative.

3x−13≤x+1⇒2x≤14⇒x≤73(x+1)<4x+2⇒3x+3<4x+2⇒x>11<x≤7\begin{aligned} 3x-13 \le x+1 &\Rightarrow 2x \le 14 \Rightarrow x \le 7\\ 3(x+1) < 4x+2 &\Rightarrow 3x+3 < 4x+2 \Rightarrow x > 1\\ 1 < x &\le 7 \end{aligned}

Answer: 1 < x ≤ 7. Number line: open circle at 1, filled circle at 7, line between.

Q14(x² + 1) to the power (2x − 3) = 1Taught · 4 marks · Indices

Taught. Shown the model first; right on the retry.

Question

Solve the equation (x² + 1) to the power (2x − 3) = 1. [4]

The question as printed

A power equals 1 in two ways: the power is 0, or the base is 1.

2x−3=0⇒x=32x2+1=1⇒x=0\begin{aligned} 2x-3 = 0 &\Rightarrow x = \tfrac32\\ x^2+1 = 1 &\Rightarrow x = 0 \end{aligned}

Answer: x = 0 or x = 3 ÷ 2

Q17Lines 3x − y + 1 = 0, x = 4, 10x + 4y = 37Still open · 5 marks · Coordinates

Question

Three lines, l₁, l₂ and l₃, are shown in the diagram. Lines l₂ and l₃ intersect at point K.

(a) The equations of the three lines are given to be 3x − y + 1 = 0, x = 4 and 10x + 4y = 37. Write down the equation of the line that corresponds to l₁, l₂ and l₃ respectively. [2]

(b) Hence, find the coordinates of K. [3]

The question as printed
3x−y+1=0⇒y=3x+1  (slopes up)10x+4y=37⇒y=−2.5x+9.25  (slopes down)10x+4(3x+1)=3722x+4=3722x=33⇒x=1.5y=3(1.5)+1=5.5\begin{aligned} 3x-y+1=0 &\Rightarrow y = 3x+1 \;(\text{slopes up})\\ 10x+4y=37 &\Rightarrow y = -2.5x+9.25 \;(\text{slopes down})\\ 10x+4(3x+1) &= 37\\ 22x+4 &= 37\\ 22x &= 33 \Rightarrow x = 1.5\\ y &= 3(1.5)+1 = 5.5 \end{aligned}

Q18P(2, 6), Q(−1, 2), R(2, 2), T(−3, 2)Wrong before · 5 marks · Coordinates

Question

On the axes shown, P is (2, 6), Q is (−1, 2), R is (2, 2) and T is (−3, 2).

(a) Find the gradient of PQ. [1]

(b) Find the equation of PQ. [1]

(c) Find the value of sin ∠QPR, giving your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms. [2]

(d) Find the value of cos ∠PQT, giving your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms. [1]

The question as printed
m=6−22−(−1)=436=43(2)+c⇒c=6−83=103PQ=32+42=5sin⁡∠QPR=QRPQ=35cos⁡∠PQT=−cos⁡∠PQR=−35\begin{aligned} m &= \frac{6-2}{2-(-1)} = \frac43\\ 6 &= \tfrac43(2)+c \Rightarrow c = 6-\tfrac83 = \tfrac{10}{3}\\ PQ &= \sqrt{3^2+4^2} = 5\\ \sin\angle QPR &= \frac{QR}{PQ} = \frac35\\ \cos\angle PQT &= -\cos\angle PQR = -\frac35 \end{aligned}

Angle PQT is on the straight line TQR, so it is 180° − angle PQR, and cos changes sign.

Q19x² + 2x + 4Still open · 5 marks · Quadratics

Still open. 27 and 30 Sep: turning point given as x only; sketch drawn below the axis; minus sign dropped from (−3, 1).

Question

(a) Express x² + 2x + 4 in the form (x + p)² + q. [1]

(b) State the turning point of the curve y = x² + 2x + 4. [1]

(c) What does the turning point in part (b) imply about the curve y = x² + 2x + 4 with respect to the x-axis? Explain your answer. [1]

(d) Sketch the graph of y = x² + 2x + 4 on the axes. Indicate clearly the coordinates of the point where the graph crosses the y-axis and the turning point on the curve. [2]

The question as printed

Half of 2 is 1; take away 1².

x2+2x+4=(x+1)2−1+4=(x+1)2+3\begin{aligned} x^2+2x+4 &= (x+1)^2-1+4\\ &= (x+1)^2+3 \end{aligned}
  • (b) Turning point as a pair: (−1, 3).
  • (c) The lowest point is at y = 3, above the x-axis, so the curve never meets it.
  • (d) x across, y up. Mark (0, 4) and (−1, 3). U-shape with its bottom at (−1, 3).

Answer: (a) (x + 1)² + 3   (b) (−1, 3)

(c) wrong before. (a)(b) right on his own. (c) added the outside angles; right on the retry.

Question

In the diagram, FA is parallel to GD. Angle FAB = 65°, angle BAE = y°, angle ABC = x°, angle at E = 150°, angle at D = 70°, and angle BCG = 45°.

(a) State the sum of interior angles of pentagon ABCDE. [1]

(b) Find angle BCD, giving a reason for your answer. [1]

(c) Find the value of x and of y. [2]

The question as printed
(5−2)×180∘=540∘∠BCD=180∘−45∘=135∘x=65∘+45∘=110∘y=540∘−110∘−135∘−70∘−150∘=75∘\begin{aligned} (5-2)\times180^\circ &= 540^\circ\\ \angle BCD &= 180^\circ-45^\circ = 135^\circ\\ x &= 65^\circ+45^\circ = 110^\circ\\ y &= 540^\circ-110^\circ-135^\circ-70^\circ-150^\circ = 75^\circ \end{aligned}

a=2510=2.5v=25−2515×9=1012×10×25=12525×25=62512×15×25=187.5\begin{aligned} a &= \frac{25}{10} = 2.5\\ v &= 25-\frac{25}{15}\times9 = 10\\ \tfrac12\times10\times25 &= 125\\ 25\times25 &= 625\\ \tfrac12\times15\times25 &= 187.5 \end{aligned}

Q22Squares ABCD and DEFG, EAB a straight lineWrong before · 6 marks · Congruence

Wrong before. Did not know how the first time. On the retry all three reasons were written; (c) rounded 1.96 to 2.

Question

In the diagram, ABCD and DEFG are squares of different sizes. EAB is a straight line.

(a) Show that angle ADE = angle CDG. [1]

(b) Prove that triangles ADE and CDG are congruent. Give a reason for each statement you make. [2]

(c) Given that DE = 6 cm and angle DEA = 50°, find the length of GB. [3]

The question as printed

(a) Angle ADE = 90° − angle ADG, and angle CDG = 90° − angle ADG, so they are equal.

(b)

  • AD = CD (sides of square ABCD)
  • DE = DG (sides of square DEFG)
  • Angle ADE = angle CDG (from (a))

Triangle ADE is congruent to triangle CDG (SAS).

(c) DE = 6 cm, angle DEA = 50°.

AD=6sin⁡50∘=4.5963AE=6cos⁡50∘=3.8567CG=AE  (congruent),CB=AD  (square)GB=4.5963−3.8567=0.7396\begin{aligned} AD &= 6\sin50^\circ = 4.5963\\ AE &= 6\cos50^\circ = 3.8567\\ CG &= AE \;(\text{congruent}),\quad CB = AD \;(\text{square})\\ GB &= 4.5963-3.8567 = 0.7396 \end{aligned}

Answer: (c) GB = 0.740 cm

Exam card: Paper 1, Thursday 1 October, 0830 to 1030

Before you start
Calculator in degrees: cos 60° = 0.5.

Every question

  1. Copy the numbers from the question, not from memory. Check your first line against the question.
  2. Write something for every part: a formula, the numbers, or a diagram.
  3. Finish with the answer line: Word = number unit.
    AB = 6.19 cm
    Mass = 1720 g
    x = 3 ÷ 2
  4. One clean line. Never scribble. A wrong line stays; the new one goes underneath.
  5. Could this answer be true? A length cannot be negative. A price of $0.002 is wrong.

Rounding to 3 significant figures
Write the full calculator value. Underline the third figure. Look at the next digit.
1.96459 ==> 1.96
3486.67 ==> 3490
8054.42 ==> 8050
The size stays the same.

The whole answer
A turning point is a pair: (−1, 3).
Factorise completely keeps the number in front: 3(x + 3)(2x − 3).
Two angles from sine: 41.2° and 180° − 41.2° = 138.8°.
A number line: open circle for <, filled circle for ≤.

Percentage change
Change ÷ original × 100.

Gradient
Up ÷ across.

Sector
Area = (angle ÷ 360) × πr²
Arc = (angle ÷ 360) × 2πr
Perimeter = arc + two radii

Geometry reasons, write them in full
Alternate angles, AB is parallel to CD.
Co-interior angles: angle X + angle Y = 180°.
Angles on a straight line add to 180°.
SAS, ASA, SSS: letters in matching order.
